title: Four Thinking Skills Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Classify eight school activities as decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, or algorithmic thinking.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify eight student activities as decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, or algorithmic thinking, correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, and algorithmic thinking, from the section "Teaching Thinking with AI" in Chapter 12

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, get feedback with the reason, and review what was missed
keyQuestions: What is the defining move in this activity?
commonMisconceptions: Any step-by-step activity is an algorithm
Abstraction means making something harder to understand
Breaking a task into steps is the same as writing an algorithm
assessmentOpportunities: A student lists the steps to make a sandwich so a robot could follow them. Which skill?
Is every step-by-step activity an algorithm?
Does abstraction make a problem harder to understand?

controls.name: Choice buttons
controls.description: commit an answer. A wrong first answer gives a hint and lets you choose again; only the first answer counts.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: opens or closes the reference table. Reading it is exploration, not evidence.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next item after feedback. On the results screen, Previous missed and Next missed step through what you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: starts a practice run with the items reshuffled. Practice runs do not change the first-run score.
